security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, metadata links, and ordinary API documentation. The setup still downloads and executes a remote package, stores authentication state, and modifies supported client configuration.

remediation.issue: The primary setup path executes a remote package without verifying its checksum.
remediation.suggestion: Make the checksum-verified download the default setup path, or add automatic integrity verification before npx executes the package.

remediation.issue: The installer changes authentication state and client configuration.
remediation.suggestion: Request explicit confirmation before each client change and clearly list affected files and settings before installation.

semantic_findings.title: Unverified Remote Package Execution
semantic_findings.description: The primary setup command tells users to execute a remote package through npx without checksum verification. A compromised release asset or hosting account could execute attacker-controlled installer code.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command explicitly uses npx with automatic confirmation on an HTTPS package URL. A separate verified workflow exists, but the primary command does not use it.

semantic_findings.title: Installer Changes Authentication and Client Configuration

semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The skill explicitly states that the CLI stores a session record, detects supported clients, and installs the bridge, skill, and configuration.

content.user_title: Access AI Models and APIs Through SandBase
content.value_statement: Using many AI providers requires separate integrations, keys, and billing workflows. SandBase offers one MCP interface for inference, media, search, scraping, and structured APIs.
actual_capabilities: Search more than 2,000 available AI models and API endpoints by query, type, or vendor.
Inspect endpoint input schemas, pricing, and execution templates before making a paid call.
Run synchronous model inference, media generation, search, scraping, and structured data requests.
Poll asynchronous jobs and retrieve completed video, scraping, or other long-running results.
List recent SandBase calls with their status and cost.
Check the connected SandBase account balance without a paid request.
limitations: Requires a SandBase account, browser authentication, and an installed local MCP bridge.
Model and API calls may incur charges and depend on upstream provider availability.
Asynchronous endpoints require repeated polling before results are available.
It should not replace local tools or dedicated integrations the user already has.

use_cases.title: Prototype Multimodal Features
use_cases.description: Discover and compare available image, video, audio, and language endpoints before integrating one into a prototype.

use_cases.title: Collect Structured Web Data
use_cases.description: Find suitable search, scraping, or social data endpoints and run small, schema-validated requests.

use_cases.title: Control AI Service Costs
use_cases.description: Inspect prices, check account balance, and review recent call costs across supported providers.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Suitable Tool
prompt_templates.prompt: Use SandBase to find tools for [task]. Show the most relevant options, their vendors, and their model types. Do not run anything yet.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Before Running
prompt_templates.prompt: Discover a SandBase endpoint for [task], inspect its schema and pricing, then summarize required inputs and expected cost before execution.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Small Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Find and inspect a SandBase endpoint for [task]. Run one request with a small limit using [inputs], then summarize the result and cost.

prompt_templates.title: Manage an Async Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Select and inspect an asynchronous SandBase endpoint for [task]. Confirm pricing, run it with [inputs], poll until completion, and report result, status, and cost.

output_examples.input: Find a Twitter search tool for AI agent posts, but do not run it.
output_examples.output: Recommended endpoint: Twitter web search timeline. It supports keyword search and returns structured posts. Inspect its schema and price before execution.

output_examples.input: Generate one fast image of a mountain lake and report the cost.
output: Selected a fast Flux image endpoint after checking its input schema and fixed per-call price.
The image request completed successfully. The response includes the generated media result and the charged amount.

output_examples.input: Check my five most recent SandBase calls.
output_examples.output: The recent-call summary lists each model or API, completion status, and recorded cost for the five latest requests.

best_practices: Discover endpoints first, then inspect the selected schema and pricing before execution.
Start search and scraping requests with small limits to validate result quality and cost.
Use the provided execution template and report costs when budget affects the task.
anti_patterns: Do not guess endpoint names or parameters without inspecting the current schema.
Do not use SandBase when the task is entirely local or the user selected another tool.
Do not start repeated paid calls without checking pricing, limits, and account balance.

faq.question: What does SandBase provide?
faq.answer: It provides one MCP interface for hosted AI models, media tools, search, scraping, embeddings, social data, and structured APIs.

faq.question: Do I need provider API keys?
faq.answer: No provider keys are required. You need a SandBase account and must complete browser authentication for the local MCP connection.

faq.question: How do I know an endpoint's inputs?
faq.answer: Run the inspection tool after discovery. It returns the input schema, pricing details, and an execution template.

faq.question: Can calls incur charges?
faq.answer: Yes. Pricing may be token-based or per call. Inspect pricing and check your balance before running costly workloads.

faq.question: How are long-running requests handled?
faq.answer: Some requests return a run identifier. Poll that run until it reports completion or failure.

faq.question: When should I avoid SandBase?
faq.answer: Avoid it for local-only tasks, when the user selected another tool, or when an existing dedicated integration already meets the need.
